prediction.text:
Alphabet said the increase in purchases of property and equipment was primarily driven by investments in technical infrastructure. Capital expenditures rose from $32.3 billion in 2023 to $52.5 billion in 2024, an increase of about 62.9%, or $20.28 billion. Alphabet describes this infrastructure as servers, network equipment and data centers. It expects to increase that investment further relative to 2024, in particular in support of AI products and services.
Alphabet's capital expenditures were $32.25 billion in FY2023.
Alphabet's capital expenditures were $52.5 billion in FY2024.
Capex grew about 62.9% from FY2023 to FY2024.
The absolute increase in capex was about $20.28 billion.
Alphabet stated that the increase in purchases of property and equipment is primarily driven by investments in technical infrastructure.
Alphabet said it invests in land, buildings, and servers and network equipment, through purchases of property and equipment and lease arrangements, to provide capacity for the growth of its services and products.
Alphabet expects to increase its investment in technical infrastructure, including servers, network equipment, and data centers, relative to 2024. It said this is to support the growth of its business and its long-term initiatives, in particular in support of AI products and services.

caveats: Only Item 7 was searched. The continuation of the 'Capital Expenditures' subsection, which lists the major spending categories, was not retrieved, so no finer causal breakdown of the $20.3 billion increase is available.
The AI-related rationale comes from Alphabet's forward-looking statement about 2025 investment, not from an explicit statement of the cause of the 2024 increase.
